# ci/cd: split release builds across runners instead of capping parallelism

## Motivation

The release job builds four targets (`darwin`/`linux` × `amd64`/`arm64`) on a
single runner, and GoReleaser starts all of them at once. A cold cross-compile
of this module peaks at about 5 GB of resident memory — `gotd` is a single
generated package holding the whole Telegram API — so four at once overruns the
16 GB hosted runner and the kernel kills the job without printing an error.

Failure reference: [Continuous delivery, September 22, 2026](https://github.com/octopot/indexit/actions/runs/35754753213).

```text
• building binaries
  • building  paths=. binaries=indexit target=darwin_arm64_v8.0
  • building  paths=. binaries=indexit target=linux_amd64_v1
  • building  paths=. binaries=indexit target=linux_arm64_v8.0
  • building  paths=. binaries=indexit target=darwin_amd64_v1
<3m34s of silence, job fails, post steps skipped>
```

`--parallelism 2` is in place as a stopgap. It halves the peak and keeps the
job inside the runner, but it is a ceiling, not a design: memory per target
only grows, and every new target makes the single runner a tighter fit while
adding a full build to one machine's wall clock.

One target per runner is the shape that scales — adding a platform becomes a
matrix entry rather than a memory calculation.

## Out of scope

- Reverting `--parallelism 2` before a replacement is green.
- The same ceiling in `make go-dist-check`, which is generated from
  `octomation/makefiles`.

## Verification PoC

The cost of a single cold target, on which the 16 GB estimate rests:

```sh
/usr/bin/time -l env CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 \
  go build -a -trimpath -ldflags '-s -w' -o /dev/null .
#      19.81 real
#      4994465792  maximum resident set size
```

GoReleaser's own split and merge is Pro-only, verified against the version the
workflow pins, v2.18.2:

```sh
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=publish --split
# ⨯ command failed   error=unknown flag: --split

# with `builder: prebuilt` in the config
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=publish
# ⨯ release failed   error=yaml: unmarshal errors:
#   line 9: field prebuilt not found in type config.Build
```

Both features carry the `g_featpro` marker in the v2.18.2 documentation
sources, so the decision below is a licensing one, not a configuration one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide between a GoReleaser Pro licence (`partial: {by: target}`,
      a matrix, `goreleaser continue --merge`) and a hand-rolled matrix of
      `goreleaser build --single-target` jobs feeding a release job.
- [ ] If hand-rolled: archives, `checksums.txt` and the Homebrew cask keep
      their current shape, including completions generated by running the
      built binary.
- [ ] Adding a target is a matrix entry only — no change to memory ceilings.
- [ ] A tagged release and a snapshot run both pass, with no job exceeding the
      runner's memory.

<!-- 2026-09-24T15:56Z https://github.com/octopot/indexit/issues/105#issuecomment-5817549098
Status 2026-09-24: the split is parked; a warm build cache comes first.

Why: the release job almost always cross-compiled cold. setup-go restores only on an exact key (it hashed `go.sum` + `tools/go.sum`), warmup never produced that key, and the monthly cleanup drops everything. Locally, one target cold takes 21s and 4.3 GB RSS; warm with only `-X` ldflags changed, 1.6s and 0.6 GB. With a warm cache, four parallel targets fit the runner easily.

Pending commit:
- `cd.yml` restores `~/.cache/go-build` and `~/go/pkg/mod` with fallback keys and saves them after a successful run; `--parallelism 2` applies only when no cache matched at all.
- `warmup.caches.yml` builds all release targets with the same key.

Splitting across runners works with OSS GoReleaser (`--single-target` builds plus a prebuilt `tool:` shim in the release job), but it saves about a minute on top of the cache, at the cost of three jobs and a shim. Worth revisiting only for a target that a hosted Linux runner cannot build.

How to decide, on the next tag (baseline v0.1.0, run 35891180728: job 9m14s, "building binaries" 2m43s):
1. "Restore the release build cache" logs a matched key, and "Limit build parallelism on a cold cache" is skipped.
2. "building binaries" in the GoReleaser step takes under 30s with default parallelism, and no OOM.
3. After a cleanup, the warmup "Caching release builds" job succeeds and the next release still hits.

If all three hold, close this issue as not planned. If 2 fails with a matched key, reopen the split.
